In cli/src/pcluster/** and cli/setup.py, exceptions re-raised inside except blocks are not required to use `raise ... from ...` (raise-missing-from disabled).

In cli/src/pcluster/** and cli/setup.py, overriding methods may have signatures that differ from the overridden method (arguments-differ disabled).
In cli/src/pcluster/** and cli/setup.py, standalone string statements are allowed (pointless-string-statement disabled).
In cli/src/pcluster/** and cli/setup.py, catching broad exceptions such as `except Exception` is allowed (broad-except disabled).

quote: All integration tests are defined in the `integration-tests/tests` directory.
statement: In tests/integration-tests, integration test modules must be placed under tests/integration-tests/tests/.

quote: * search for `test_*.py` or `*_test.py` files... * `test_` prefixed test functions or methods outside of class * `test_` prefixed test functions or methods inside `Test` prefixed test classes (without an `__init__` method)
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests/**, test files must be named test_*.py or *_test.py, test functions must be prefixed test_, and test classes must be prefixed Test and have no __init__ method.

quote: Test cases are organized in separate files where the file name is `test_$feature_under_test`. For example test cases specific to awsbatch scheduler can be defined in a file named `test_awsbatch.py`.
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests/**, test files must be named test_<feature_under_test>.py, one file per feature (optionally grouped in a category directory).

quote: If you don't need to reference the parametrized arguments in your test case you can simply replace the function arguments with this annotation: `@pytest.mark.usefixtures("region", "os", "instance", "scheduler")`
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests/**, test functions that do not reference the region/os/instance/scheduler dimensions should declare them via @pytest.mark.usefixtures("region", "os", "instance", "scheduler") instead of as function arguments.

quote: It is possible to restrict the dimensions each test is compatible with by using some custom markers.
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests/**, tests restrict the dimensions they run on with the custom markers @pytest.mark.instances/regions/oss/schedulers/dimensions and skip_instances/skip_regions/skip_oss/skip_schedulers/skip_dimensions.

quote: To define such exceptions it is possible to extend the list `UNSUPPORTED_DIMENSIONS` in conftest_markers.py file.
statement: In tests/integration-tests, globally invalid dimension combinations must be declared by extending UNSUPPORTED_DIMENSIONS in conftest_markers.py.

quote: A fixture `test_datadir` is built on top of it and can be used to inject the `datadir` with resources for the specific test function.
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests/**, per-test resources must live in tests/<test_file>/<test_case>/ and be accessed via the test_datadir fixture (shared resources via shared_datadir from tests/data).
scope: tests/integration-tests/tests/** test functions and data dirs

quote: The cluster configuration needed for a given test case needs to reside in the test specific `test_datadir` and it needs to be in a file named pcluster.config.yaml.
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests/**, a test case's cluster configuration must reside in its test_datadir as a file named pcluster.config.yaml.

quote: Test cases can then inject a fixture called `pcluster_config_reader` which allows to automatically read and render the configuration defined for a specific test case
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests/**, test cases should load and render their cluster config via the pcluster_config_reader fixture.

quote: Cluster lifecycle management is fully managed by the testing framework and is exposed through the fixture `clusters_factory`.
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests/**, clusters must be created through the clusters_factory fixture so they are automatically destroyed.

quote: To execute remote commands or scripts on the head node of the cluster under test, the `RemoteCommandExecutor` class can be used.
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests/**, remote commands and scripts on the head node should be executed via RemoteCommandExecutor (run_remote_command / run_remote_script).

quote: If additional AWS resources are needed by the integration tests you can use a session scoped fixture, `cfn_stacks_factory`... (note: fixtures are always better to handle resources cleanup.)
statement: In tests/integration-tests, additional AWS resources should be created as CloudFormation stacks via the cfn_stacks_factory fixture (or a reduced-scope fixture), preferring fixtures over direct CfnStacksFactory use for cleanup.

quote: 1. Add `run_benchmarks` and `benchmarks` fixtures to the test ... 2. Add `benchmarks` parameter to `pcluster_config_reader`.
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests/**, tests that run performance benchmarks must take the run_benchmarks and benchmarks fixtures and pass benchmarks=benchmarks to pcluster_config_reader.

quote: Changes to the API request/response model require changes to files under `cli/src/pcluster/api/models`. ... To avoid huge diffs import only models related to your modifications.
statement: In cli/src/pcluster/api/models/**, API request/response models must be placed there, imported from the generated server stub, and only models related to the change should be imported.

quote: relevant changes need to be applied to controllers under the `cli/src/pcluster/api/controllers` directory.
statement: In cli/src/pcluster/api/controllers/**, API endpoint handlers must live there and match the controller signatures of the generated server stub.

quote: Please import the newly changes available in the generated stub to `cli/src/pcluster/api/openapi/openapi.yaml`. For each diff with the respect to the generated file please add an `#  override: reason` comment documenting why this is required.
statement: In cli/src/pcluster/api/openapi/openapi.yaml, every deviation from the generated OpenAPI spec must be annotated with an `# override: reason` comment.
